reasoning_traces.think:
The calibration integrity grade \(\mathcal{C}\) measures deviation from ideal calibration by comparing observed coverage against nominal confidence levels. It enables GSI to dynamically adjust belief states based on empirical reliability. The drift pressure index \(\mathcal{D}\) detects shifts in underlying distributions using relative entropy changes, informing when models may be outdated. The GSE signal score \(\mathcal{S}\) synthesizes these into a decision kernel combining residual consistency and role volatility. These primitives form a dual inference loop: \(\mathcal{C}\) ensures trustworthiness, \(\mathcal{D}\) flags obsolescence, and \(\mathcal{S}\) guides action. Failure modes include overfitting in \(\mathcal{C}\), false positives in \(\mathcal{D}\), and misalignment between \(\mathcal{R}\) and \(\mathcal{V}\) in \(\mathcal{S}\).
